claims.text: refund-plan-example.md lines 8-23: work similar to finished work (screens, API, email job) is sized in story points and forecast with velocity; seven items sum to 28; the retry job 'giống job gửi email' is 5 points.

Lines 27-30: the team has never called the gateway's refund API or reconciled with accounting, so no earlier work to compare points with; the two items are estimated in days of one person's work with O, M, P; one developer does both from Sprint 15.
Lines 32-36: integration O/M/P 4/6/14 → 7; reconciliation 2/4/12 → 5; the two together 12.

Lines 40-43: O-P gap of the integration is 10 days because the team knows very little about the gateway; a wide gap is information for the plan, not a bad estimate; (O + 4M + P) / 6 leans to M but is pulled toward P when P is far from M.
The weighted average (O + 4M + P) / 6 is one common way to combine three-point values; M counts four times; with O close to M and P far above, the result moves toward P.

claims.text: In the refund plan, work similar to finished stories stays in story points; three-point estimates are used for the two items the team has never done. For work with no similar finished story, a point number is only a guess; a wide O-P gap signals missing knowledge.

P is a realistic bad case with a reason you can name, not every imaginable disaster and not padding; planning at M leaves no room when P is far above M. The refund plan uses days of one person's work.
Lines 37-38 of refund-plan-example.md add a separate line of extra days (8) on top of the 12, computed from the gaps between P and M, total 20; the lesson only points to it for the next lesson.
